title: Take a contact grill's two latched plates off by both side release handles at once, and slide out its drip tray
instruction: Take both cooking plates off the grill and put them on the blue drying mat, and take the drip tray out from under the grill.
context: Washing the plates of a contact grill (a George Foreman type with removable plates) is an everyday kitchen chore. The manual: "Holding a plate with both hands, use your thumbs to pull out the release handles" (GRP106QPG Use & Care); "The grill plates may be removed from the appliance by pulling out on the grill plate release handles" (GRP3CAN); "Allow the drip tray to cool before removing it from under the grill." Each plate has a sprung release handle on its left and right side, 39 cm apart tip to tip; each handle's latch catches the grill frame until the handle is pulled out 6 mm, and it snaps back when let go. So a plate comes free only while both its handles are held out at once, which one gripper cannot do: on one handle alone the plate only tilts a little on the other latch. The upper plate stands in the open lid and must be drawn forward and turned flat; the drip tray is tucked under the body's front edge and must be slid out.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top. Grill (fixed): round stainless body 34 cm across, centre x 30.0, y 16.0, top 6.4 cm up, underside 4.0 cm up on a 25 cm pedestal; lid open upright at the back (front face x 47.5, centre 27.2 cm up). Lower plate (loose, 0.60 kg): 30 cm round cast plate, centre x 30.0, y 16.0, 8.4 cm up. Upper plate (loose, 0.60 kg): the same, standing in the lid, centre x 45.5, y 16.0, 27.2 cm up, face toward the robot. Each plate: a black release handle 4.5 x 3.9 x 2.0 cm on each side (tips 39.4 cm apart) on a 400 N/m spring, 10 mm travel. Drip tray (loose, 0.12 kg): 20 x 7 x 2.5 cm, 1 cm front lip, x 9.5-16.5, y 16.0, back 3.5 cm under the body. Drying mat (fixed): blue silicone 38 x 33 x 0.4 cm, centre x 26.0, y -24.0. Arms at the ready pose, grippers open. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Every control step, from PhysX contact forces between each plate, each handle and the tray and every link of both arms. Each plate: 0.15 once taken off by its handles (centre 3 cm or more from its seat while each handle is pressed by a gripper with 1 N or more); +0.20 when it then lies flat (within 10 degrees) on the mat or on the other plate lying there, centre over the mat, lowest point within 6 mm of what it lies on, and nothing touches it (0.1 N). A plate whose centre ever falls faster than 0.77 m/s (a 3 cm drop) gets no credit; nothing else is latched. Drip tray, 0.20: its back corners and back middle 17.5 cm or more from the body's centre (clear of the body), lowest point within 4 mm of the table, tilted under 10 degrees, untouched. 1.0 when all of that holds with no arm touching any plate, handle or the tray and everything still (under 1 mm in 1 s) for 1 s; otherwise the sum (at most 0.9). Doing nothing scores 0. Real trial: handles held and drops from the video; flat with a phone level app; the tray with a ruler.
reset_notes: Latch both plates back in (lower plate in the body, upper plate in the lid, both handles snapped in), open the lid upright, slide the drip tray back under the body's front edge, clear the mat. Simulation: each trial starts the simulator afresh.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 20 Hz control. True-size plates (30 cm, 0.60 kg; estimate) and handles; the latch is modelled as a tongue on each sprung handle hooking under a lip of the frame (6 mm overlap, 10 mm travel); spring rate and masses are estimates. The lid is fixed open (no hinge). The plates are flat cast discs with ridges, without the lower plate's sloped spout. The drip tray is straight, not curved, and empty (no grease). Grip forces and friction are simulator values.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the left gripper went down beside the lower plate's left handle and hovered there, the right turned toward the grill from beside the mat; neither took hold of a handle and nothing moved); demo: 1.0
